A span binds `[innerHtml]`, which the compiler maps to `innerHTML`, and one binds `[outerHTML]`: Angular's sanitizer keeps a link and a `tabindex` stop in either. An iframe writes a `srcdoc`, which Angular hands over unsanitized; it is written `<xhtml:IFRAME>`, an HTML iframe all the same, which its prefix and its capitals do not hide. An `<object>` embeds a `data:` address and binds its fallback two ways, `[(innerHTML)]`. An `<embed>` embeds a page, and a `<frame>` inside a `<frameset>` another. Each may draw a stop that no point examines, and the refusal names every element and every way it draws.
